analysis: The PR is almost entirely CI workflow and documentation changes. The substantive change is in release-provider.yml: a new step computes cluster_runtime facts from the final signed app, and prepare adds --cluster-runtime when CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND is true (head ~1078-1088). Containment controls are visible in the workflow. The step deletes the signing keychain and proves the identity is gone, re-checks the bundle SHA-256 against BUNDLE_HASH, unsets r2_public_url and coordinator_url, and the docs say the CLI runs under env -i. It reads no secrets, and sending is opt-in per environment (fail-closed when enabled, warn-only otherwise). I found no regression in these controls. The main concern is trust: the facts are produced by the build itself and, according to docs/reference/configuration.md and docs/operations/provider-release.md, are turned by the coordinator into approvals, pair-serving grants and public parity qualifications. Declared qualification scope is wider than its evidence: the changelog admits no two-M5-Ultra pipeline run and no GLM tensor-parallel cross-cable record. Together with the A-005 release key this concentrates qualification authority (A-017, T-052, T-054). That is the finding above. A lower-severity docs/inference.md observation (qualification applied to the whole mode family on any Apple silicon pair, ~line 5275) was raised in unit 5 and is subsumed here. Unverified because the code was not supplied: scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, provider-cluster-runtime-models.py, the provider-release-publication.py --cluster-runtime handling, coordinator validation (platform-owned), the 30-day artifact contents, and the heartbeat-file PID guard (DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE). Cluster pairs also lose auto-update (changelog/docs), which is a patch-currency matter for T-054/T-043 and depends on platform revocation enforcement. Other docs changes (Qwen27 assistant excluded from coordinator pairing, registration-timeout ends no longer counted) are conservative or availability-related. T-041 is unaffected.

findings.detail: The new CI step (.github/workflows/release-provider.yml, head ~941-1023, CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND at ~298-308) computes cluster_runtime facts using the freshly built app's own CLI and worker. When the per-environment variable is true, they are sent in the POST /v1/releases payload. The docs say the coordinator derives cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications from that block, and that GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B qualifications come from a build-side declaration (ClusterPublicModels) resting on an owner decision. These facts are self-reported by the build and authenticated only by the release key. Anyone who can call the release API (A-005) or alter the declaration could then create public-serving qualification, not just binary trust. That weakens the independent-qualification assumption behind A-017, T-052 and T-054. The coordinator-side controls are outside the supplied evidence and unverified. Fix: record this derivation path in the threat model, and confirm the coordinator requires independent approval of the cluster_runtime block rather than trusting the release key alone.
findings.title: Release-registered cluster_runtime can mint public-traffic cluster approvals, grants and parity qualifications; threat model does not cover it
